Text: $PLTR This is an old gripe that doesn't hold water: ontology is a cohesive framework of real-time feeds from 100s of disconnected systems, logic, & functions to safely orchestrate goals. Pointing raw LLMs at disconnected relational databases is dangerous and unreliable. LLMs require an ontology to operate safely in enterprise environments. LLMs can't write software to do what it doesn't understand. LLMs are not really reasoning machines. If an LLM queries raw enterprise databases containing thousands of unmapped, non-standardized tables, it lacks the context to identify the single source of truth or business rules. Ontologies model & translate raw data into deterministic business entities. Raw LLMs can generate text or code, but they cannot execute safe transactional write-backs, which require permissions and purpose-based access control. Asking an LLM is easy. Replicating 20 years of mapped organizational logic, security policies, and operational action pipelines is not.
